text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Demands of city authorities for some four billion dinars from the republic's coffers is nothing more but a request to print money, says Serbian trade minister Srdjan Nikolic.
- Director of Yugoslavia's customs administration Mihalj Kertes accuses domestic tobacco firms of smuggling cigarettes.
- Ljubljana-Belgrade flights have been interrupted because Ljubljana's licence for landing at Belgrade's Surcin airport has expired.

- Yugoslav-Slovenian trade in 1996 stood at $127.6 million, and has increased by six percent in Q1 1997 over the same period in 1996, said representative of the Slovenian Chamber of Commerce Vinko Zupancic.
- Businessmen of China's province Lianing are arriving in Belgrade on Friday.
- There is great complementarity between Yugoslav and Romanian agricultural sectors, said the two countries' agriculture ministers in Bucharest.
- The Yugoslav government must exert pressure on the U.S. to release our assets, says Borka Vucic, acting general manager of Beogradska banka.
- The central bank will keep a stable dinar exchange rate and there should be no fear of inflation, says acting National Bank of Yugoslavia Governor Bozidar Gazivoda.
- There is no reason to hold early elections, they will be held when due, by the end of the year, says spokesman of the Socialist Party of Serbia Ivica Dacic.
- Serbian government to make proposals on Friday to resolve health strikers' demands.
- Italian financial organisation FINEST and Beobanka set up an agency Beo-Finest to fund economic development projects in Serbia.
NASA BORBA
- Over two thousand doctors and nurses protest in front of government and vow to continue until satisfactory solution is found to their demands of outstanding wages.
- It looks like wheat yields will be good this year and there will be exports through berter deals to east European markets, says Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic.
- Forum of Belgrade high schools annnounces strike for May 26 because of irregular payment of wages.
BORBA
- Yugoslav-Albanian border is secure, says Yugoslav chief of general staff General Momcilo Perisic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Large quantities of infected meat were imported in Yugoslavia during the sanctions period, says director of firm Vizelj from Padinska Skela.
- MONTENETGRO -
MONITOR

- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic and other officials of the reform wing of the Democratic Party of Socialists should use their prestige to establish wide reforms, editorial.

- President Momir Bulatovic tries to form a para-state council to put the security service under his supervision. Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic tryin to keep secret police under his own control, commentary.
- Urban planning chaos in the coastal town of Budva -- 40,000 to 50,000 square metres of housing now being built.

- (Serbian President Slobodan ) Milosevic's 1989 constitution of Serbia is anti-Yugoslav, it made all republics of the former Yugoslavia, with the exception of Montenegro, leave Serbia, says Desimir Tosic, the president of the European movement of Serbia.
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Parliament will continue its session on Tuesday. The parliament adopted the 1996 final budget statetment and now has a draft law on the security council on its agenda.

- The port of Bar reached an agreement with Medex press from Genoa to set up a container line Bar-Gioia-Tauro- Malta- Pireus. The fist ship will arrive in Bar on May 26. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 43045
